Koh Samui costs more than Koh Phangan, Koh Tao or the mainland, mainly because of flights and resort prices. By our estimates from 2026 prices, a careful traveller can manage on about 1,500–2,500 THB a day, mid-range travellers spend 4,000–7,000 THB and luxury starts around 15,000 THB, per person, excluding flights. Street dishes cost 50–120 THB, a one-hour Thai massage 300–500 THB, a scooter 150–350 THB a day, and an Ang Thong speedboat day 1,800 THB plus the 300 THB park fee.

Daily budget at a glance

Estimate, 2026: per person per day, sharing a double room, excluding flights. Activities are averaged over the trip (a boat day every two or three days).

Budget means a guesthouse in Maenam or Lamai, street food and markets, songthaews and a rented scooter. Mid-range means a beach hotel in Chaweng, Bophut or Lamai, restaurant meals, Grab and taxis. Luxury means a resort or pool villa, private transfers and private boat days.

Getting there

Flights are the biggest single cost for most visitors, and the reason Samui is dearer than its neighbours. Bangkok Airways operates every domestic route into Samui Airport, so there is no low-cost competition on the direct flight.

Route from BangkokTimeOne way (THB, approx.)
Direct flight to Samui (USM)1 h 05–1 h 10 flight2,800–6,800, checked bag included
Low-cost flight to Surat Thani + coach + ferry5–7 h door to door1,500–3,000 all-in
Night train + bus + ferry15–17 h950–2,000
Bus + ferry12–16 h620–1,750

For a couple, the Surat Thani route can save 2,000–6,000 THB each way against a peak-date direct flight, at the cost of most of a day. Book direct flights early for Christmas, New Year and Songkran. Compare routes in Bangkok to Koh Samui and how to get to Koh Samui.

Accommodation by area and season

Rooms are the second-biggest cost and vary more by area and date than anything else. Maenam is the cheapest beachfront (mid-range 1,000–2,500 THB), Lamai the best value on the east coast (1,500–3,500 THB), Chaweng mid-priced with budget options back from the beach (2,000–4,500 THB, guesthouses 500–950 THB), and Bophut and Choeng Mon the dearest mid-range areas (2,500–7,000 THB). Luxury resorts start around 10,000 THB a night.

  • Peak seasons: mid-December to February and July–August, when rates run 30–80% above shoulder-season prices. Christmas and New Year are the dearest nights of the year.
  • Shoulder: March–April (except Songkran), May–June and September.
  • Cheapest: October and November, the rainy season.
  • Long stays: monthly rentals in Maenam, Lamai and Bophut are much cheaper per night than hotels, but electricity is usually billed per unit on top.

Compare areas in where to stay on Koh Samui, and villas in Koh Samui villas.

Food and drink

Eating is where Samui can be cheap or expensive depending on where you sit. A street dish costs 50–120 THB; the same pad thai on a beachfront terrace can cost three or four times as much. Night markets are the best value: Lamai Night Market (daily, by the river bridge), Si Khao Night Market off Chaweng Beach Road (17:00–23:00), Nathon's night food market (16:30–22:00) and Fisherman's Village Walking Street on Fridays. A filling market dinner with a drink is about 300–500 THB.

Local beer (Chang, Leo) costs 60–100 THB in shops and simple bars; beach clubs and resort bars charge much more. Happy hours in Fisherman's Village and Chaweng bring cocktails down to around 99 THB.

Service charge and VAT: prices followed by "++" (common in resorts, upmarket restaurants and spas) add a 10% service charge and then 7% VAT, so a 1,000++ THB dinner costs about 1,177 THB. Street stalls and local restaurants quote net prices. Tipping is not expected at street stalls; rounding up or leaving 20–50 THB is appreciated in restaurants that don't add service. See restaurants and markets.

Transport

  • Taxis: no meters; airport fares roughly 400–700 THB per car depending on zone; a full day 2,000–3,000 THB. Agree the price first.
  • Grab: usually cheaper than street taxis; short hops 80–120 THB, cross-island 200–350 THB, airport runs 300–600 THB. Prices surge in rain.
  • Songthaews: the cheapest way along the ring road, 30–80 THB locally, cash only, by day.
  • Scooters: 150–350 THB a day, plus fuel. Only ride with an International Driving Permit covering motorcycles; without it your insurance will usually not pay, which makes a crash very expensive.
  • Cars: 800–1,200 THB a day for a compact, sensible for families and the west coast.

Cash or card?

You need both. Visa and Mastercard are accepted in malls, supermarkets, 7-Eleven, hotels, most sit-down restaurants and spas, and our tours are paid online by card and charged in THB. Cash is needed for street food and market stalls, songthaews, many taxis, small guesthouses, massage shops, parking, and every island and park fee on boat trips. A practical approach is to pay big bills (hotel, tours, restaurants) by card and carry 2,000–3,000 THB in cash for the day, more on boat days.

When paying by card or withdrawing cash, always choose to be charged in THB. If a machine offers to convert to your home currency, decline: the "guaranteed" rate is worse than your bank's. Exchange booths in Chaweng, Lamai and Bophut give fair rates for clean euro, dollar and sterling notes.

Budgeting for families

Families spend less per person than couples because children share rooms and pay less on tours. On our boat trips, children aged 3–11 pay the child price (for example 1,100 THB on the Ang Thong big boat, 1,250 THB on Pig Island and 1,600 THB on the Koh Tao trip) and infants aged 0–2 travel free. Park fees for children are 150 THB at Ang Thong. Family rooms and two-bedroom pool villas in Choeng Mon, Maenam and the west coast often work out cheaper than two hotel rooms. A rented car (800–1,200 THB a day) is usually cheaper than taxis for a family of four. See Koh Samui with kids.

When Samui is cheapest

October and November are the cheapest months for rooms, because they are the wettest. Ang Thong is closed from 1 November to 15 December, but Pig Island runs all year and the island is green and quiet. For better weather at moderate prices, aim for May–June or September, or March and April outside Songkran. The dearest period is from about 20 December to early January, when rooms, flights and transfers all peak. See weather by month and Koh Samui in November.

Money-saving tips

  • Use AEON ATMs inside Big C and Lotus's (150 THB fee instead of 220–250 THB) and withdraw larger amounts less often.
  • Decline dynamic currency conversion at ATMs and card machines; always pay in THB.
  • Eat at markets and local restaurants rather than on beachfront terraces.
  • Ride songthaews by day along the ring road (30–80 THB) instead of taxis.
  • Travel in the shoulder months (March–April, May–June, September) for good weather at lower rates.
  • Choose Pig Island as your boat day if money is tight: at 1,450 THB it is our lowest-priced shared boat trip and runs all year.
  • Do the free sights: Big Buddha, Wat Plai Laem, Hin Ta and Hin Yai, Wat Khunaram, Lad Koh viewpoint and Na Muang Waterfall 1 cost nothing beyond parking.
  • Base yourself in Lamai or Maenam and visit Chaweng for a night out.
  • Refill a water bottle at your hotel or at refill stations rather than buying plastic bottles every few hours.
  • Buy a tourist SIM (499 THB for 8 days) rather than paying roaming charges.
  • Share a private boat with friends: our private longtail to Pig Island costs 5,950 THB per boat for up to 8 people, about 745 THB each when full.

Hidden costs

  • Park and island fees in cash: Ang Thong 300 THB per adult and 150 THB per child, Koh Nang Yuan 250 THB, Koh Madsum about 50 THB. They are rarely included in tour prices.
  • Remote pickup: +400 THB per person, return, from Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut on most tours.
  • ATM fees: 220–250 THB per withdrawal adds up over a fortnight.
  • "++" prices: +10% service and +7% VAT on resort menus, spas and some restaurants.
  • Peak surcharges: 30–80% on rooms from mid-December to February and in July–August; gala dinners on Christmas and New Year's Eve.
  • Towing: scooters parked on the road at Fisherman's Village on Friday evenings are towed, and release costs 500 THB or more. Park at The Wharf (about 20 THB for a scooter).
  • Parking and small entry fees: 20–60 THB at waterfalls and sights; some private viewpoints charge entry.
  • Scooter damage claims: photograph the bike before you ride, and never leave your passport as a deposit. See scams to avoid.
  • Departure: there is no separate departure tax to pay at Samui Airport; airport charges are included in your ticket, but airside food and drink cost more than in town.
  • Medical costs: private hospitals are expensive without insurance. See travel insurance.
